name: HAProxy
tagline: Load balances TCP and HTTP with health checks, SNI routing and a floating IP.

howItWorks.title: What it is and where it sits
howItWorks.body:
HAProxy is a high-performance TCP and HTTP load balancer and reverse proxy.
mode tcp works at L4: it relays bytes and never reads the payload.
mode http works at L7: it parses requests, rewrites headers and routes by content.
It sits in the Edge layer in front of app servers, databases or cluster nodes.
TLS can pass through untouched or terminate on the balancer.

howItWorks.title: Architecture and config model
howItWorks.body:
Config sections: global, defaults, frontend, backend, plus listen for combined blocks.
A frontend binds addresses and applies rules; the first matching use_backend wins.
A backend holds servers, a balance algorithm and health checks.
Multi-threaded workers share one process; nbthread follows the CPU count.
Master-worker mode lets a reload start new workers and drain the old ones.

howItWorks.title: Request flow
howItWorks.body:
The kernel accepts the connection; a worker thread binds it to a frontend.
ACLs evaluate in order on SNI, Host header, path or method.
http-request rules can deny, redirect or rewrite before backend selection.
The balancer picks a healthy server below its maxconn; extra requests queue.
SNI routing at L4 needs tcp-request inspect-delay to read the ClientHello.
Use L4 for databases and the Kubernetes API; L7 for web and APIs.

howItWorks.title: Balancing and health checks
howItWorks.body:
roundrobin spreads evenly; leastconn suits long-lived sessions; uri hashes the request path.
check probes with a TCP connect; option httpchk GET /healthz tests the application.
inter, fall and rise set probe speed and flap tolerance.
backup servers take traffic only when all primaries are down.
Stick tables track request rates; use them for rate limiting.

howItWorks.title: High availability and scaling
howItWorks.body:
Two nodes share one VIP through keepalived VRRP, IP protocol 112.
The highest priority holds the VIP; a track_script lowers it when haproxy dies.
The BACKUP claims the VIP and sends gratuitous ARP.
Keep both nodes on identical haproxy.cfg from Git.
Scale a single node vertically first; HAProxy handles very high connection counts per host.

howItWorks.title: Security and observability
howItWorks.body:
Bind the stats socket and page to localhost or admin networks only.
http-request deny restricts paths such as /admin to internal networks.
Built-in Prometheus exporter on /metrics (2.4 and newer) and a stats page at /stats.
tcplog and httplog record timers that separate queue, connect and response time.
Alert on 5xx rate, backend queue depth, servers down and session rate against maxconn.

howItWorks.title: Failure modes and troubleshooting
howItWorks.body:
All servers failing health checks returns 503; check the stats page for L4 and L7 check reasons.
Termination state codes in the log, such as sD or cD, show which side timed out.
haproxy -c catches config errors; a bad reload leaves the old workers serving.
Idle long-lived sessions die at timeout server; raise timeout tunnel for WebSockets and databases.
Runtime API via the stats socket drains a server: set server be/srv state drain.

howItWorks.title: Connecting to its neighbours
howItWorks.body:
In front (Users): DNS points at the HAProxy VIP, or a cloud balancer forwards to it.
Behind, on VMs (Infrastructure): backends hold app servers and databases, each with a health check.
Behind, on Kubernetes (Platform): list every worker node IP and the NodePort as servers, with check.
Service type LoadBalancer: a cloud balancer or MetalLB gives a VIP; HAProxy can sit behind it or replace it on-prem.
Control plane: mode tcp on 6443 across all API servers gives kubectl one stable endpoint.
The HAProxy Kubernetes Ingress Controller can run inside the cluster instead and route by Host and path.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
NGINX: choose it when you also serve static files or want one tool for web and proxy.
Envoy: choose it for dynamic xDS config, gRPC and mesh data planes.
Traefik: choose it for automatic Kubernetes and container discovery.
Caddy: choose it for automatic HTTPS and a short config.
Cloud load balancers: choose them when the provider should run the Edge and its HA.

flow: The client connects to the VIP held by the MASTER node.
A HAProxy worker thread accepts the connection on a frontend.
tcp-request inspect-delay waits for the TLS ClientHello and reads the SNI.
ACLs run in order; use_backend or default_backend picks the pool.
The balance algorithm chooses a healthy server below maxconn.
Servers can be VMs, Kubernetes NodePorts or API servers on 6443.
A NodePort hit is forwarded by kube-proxy to a ready pod.
Counters and logs update; health checks run in the background.

deploy.summary: Run HAProxy in Docker, then add keepalived on two hosts for a floating IP.
prerequisites: Two Linux hosts on one L2 subnet, one free VIP
Docker Engine and the keepalived package

steps.title: Write haproxy.cfg (VM pools, API servers, NodePorts)
steps.code:
global
    log stdout format raw local0
    maxconn 20000
    stats socket /tmp/haproxy.sock mode 660 level admin expose-fd listeners

defaults
    mode tcp
    log global
    option tcplog
    timeout connect 3s
    timeout client  1m
    timeout server  1m
    timeout check   2s

frontend stats
    mode http
    bind :8404
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 5s
    http-request use-service prometheus-exporter if { path /metrics }

frontend fe_https
    bind :443
    tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
    tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }
    use_backend be_app_a if { req_ssl_sni -i a.example.test }
    use_backend be_app_b if { req_ssl_sni -i b.example.test }
    default_backend be_app_a

backend be_app_a
    balance roundrobin
    default-server inter 2s fall 3 rise 2
    server a1 10.0.1.11:443 check
    server a2 10.0.1.12:443 check

backend be_app_b
    balance leastconn
    default-server inter 2s fall 3 rise 2
    server b1 10.0.2.11:443 check
    server b2 10.0.2.12:443 check backup

frontend fe_http
    mode http
    bind :80
    option httplog
    acl is_api path_beg /api
    acl is_admin path_beg /admin
    acl internal src 10.0.0.0/8
    http-request deny if is_admin !internal
    use_backend be_api if is_api
    default_backend be_web

backend be_api
    mode http
    balance uri
    option httpchk GET /healthz
    http-check expect status 200
    server api1 10.0.3.11:8080 check
    server api2 10.0.3.12:8080 check

backend be_web
    mode http
    balance roundrobin
    server web1 10.0.4.11:8080 check
    server web2 10.0.4.12:8080 check

frontend fe_k8s_api
    bind :6443
    default_backend be_k8s_api

backend be_k8s_api
    balance roundrobin
    default-server inter 3s fall 3 rise 2
    server cp1 10.0.20.21:6443 check
    server cp2 10.0.20.22:6443 check
    server cp3 10.0.20.23:6443 check

frontend fe_nodeport
    bind :8080
    default_backend be_nodeport

backend be_nodeport
    balance leastconn
    default-server inter 2s fall 3 rise 2
    server w1 10.0.20.11:30080 check
    server w2 10.0.20.12:30080 check
    server w3 10.0.20.13:30080 check
steps.note: Replace every address and the NodePort. The Prometheus exporter needs HAProxy 2.4 or newer.

steps.title: Validate the configuration
steps.note: Require exit code 0 before every reload.

steps.title: Run HAProxy in Docker
steps.code:
docker run -d --name haproxy --restart unless-stopped \
  --sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 \
  -p 80:80 -p 443:443 -p 6443:6443 -p 8080:8080 -p 127.0.0.1:8404:8404 \
  -v "$PWD/haproxy.cfg:/usr/local/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg:ro" \
  haproxy:3.0
docker logs haproxy --tail 20
steps.note: The image runs unprivileged, so the sysctl frees ports below 1024. Pin the minor tag you tested.

steps.title: Reload gracefully
steps.code:
docker kill -s USR2 haproxy
# package install:
# sudo haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg && sudo systemctl reload haproxy
steps.note: The image runs master-worker mode; SIGUSR2 starts a new worker and drains the old one.

steps.title: Prepare both nodes for keepalived
steps.code:
sudo apt-get install -y keepalived
echo 'net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind = 1' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/90-haproxy.conf
sudo sysctl --system
sudo iptables -I INPUT -p 112 -d 224.0.0.18 -j ACCEPT
steps.note: Run on both nodes; keepalived stays on the host, not in the container. Persist the firewall rule with your normal tooling.

steps.title: keepalived.conf on the MASTER
steps.note: Put this in /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf. On the BACKUP change only state BACKUP and priority 100.

steps.title: Start keepalived
steps.code:
sudo systemctl enable --now keepalived
ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep 192.0.2.100
steps.note: The VIP appears on the MASTER only. Both nodes need the same virtual_router_id, password and haproxy.cfg.

steps.title: Test failover
steps.code:
ping -c 20 192.0.2.100 &
sudo systemctl stop keepalived   # on the MASTER
ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep 192.0.2.100   # on the BACKUP
steps.note: The VIP should move within a few seconds. Decide between preempt (default) and nopreempt.

verify: Config: haproxy -c -f haproxy.cfg exits 0 and prints 'Configuration file is valid'.
Stats: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8404/stats;csv' | cut -d, -f1,2,18 shows UP servers.
Metrics: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8404/metrics returns Prometheus text.
SNI: openssl s_client -connect VIP:443 -servername a.example.test </dev/null reaches backend A.
HA: ip addr shows the VIP on the MASTER, then on the BACKUP after the stop.
pitfalls: Missing inspect-delay: SNI ACLs see an empty buffer and everything hits default_backend.
A health check on the wrong port marks healthy servers down.
Missing timeouts leak idle connections; set connect, client and server.
Idle database or WebSocket sessions die at timeout server; raise timeout tunnel.
Different virtual_router_id or two MASTERs cause split brain, with the VIP on both.
Clouds and filtered VLANs drop VRRP and gratuitous ARP; failover silently never happens.
Unresolvable DNS names fail the reload; use resolvers with init-addr none.
keyPoints: Frontends match traffic; backends balance it across health-checked servers.
L4 passes TLS untouched and routes by SNI; L7 routes by Host and path.
One config file, validated with haproxy -c, reloads without dropping connections.
keepalived VRRP floats one IP between two HAProxy nodes.
quickDeploy: Write haproxy.cfg and validate it with haproxy -c.
Run the pinned HAProxy image in Docker.
Add keepalived on two nodes; stop the MASTER to test.
osiNote: Balances TCP at L4 and routes HTTP by host and path at L7.
production: Set maxconn and timeouts; load test at twice peak.
Run two nodes with keepalived; kill the MASTER to prove failover.
Keep haproxy.cfg in Git; validate with haproxy -c, then reload.
Restrict stats and admin sockets; deny /admin outside internal subnets.
Scrape /metrics; alert on 5xx rate, queue depth and servers down.
